stem:
The giant octopus lays 20,000 to 100,000 fertilized eggs. After hatching, most octopuses become prey to larger marine organisms, and less than 5% will reach adulthood to reproduce.

One benefit of the giant octopus laying many eggs is to —

options.label: F
options.text: increase the average body size for surviving individuals to avoid predation

options.label: G
options.text: decrease competition between different octopus species to maintain resources in the population

options.label: H
options.text: increase the chance that more individuals will survive to maintain the population

options.label: J
options.text: decrease the likelihood of offspring being consumed by predators
